Chaotic Playground Mayhem
Crab Game is all about fast-paced proximity chat, ridiculous physics, and absolute betrayal. The loop of surviving childish playground minigames while sliding, sprinting, and smacking other players with a stick is incredibly intense and hilarious.

It’s dead simple to pick up, but mastering the slippery movement mechanics and outsmarting 30 other screaming players takes genuine skill. Watching a crown-wearer blow up or clutching a last-second win in a game of tag never gets old.

While the toxic lobbies and frequent player-made server lag can frustrate, it is the ultimate game to jump into with a big group of friends.

If you’re looking for a free, unhinged multiplayer party game filled with nonstop screaming and funny moments, this is a must-play. 8/10

"I really wanted to like Crab Game, but it's a huge disappointment. The controls are janky and slippery as hell, making platforming infuriating. The game is full of bugs, gets extremely repetitive after a few rounds, and the community is pure cancer — constant toxicity, racism, mic spam, and hackers everywhere. Great idea, terrible execution. Not recommended."

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has graphics that are simple or poor in quality.

citations.review_text:
Free. Fun. Worth It.

Crab Game is basically a fan-made multiplayer game inspired by the Squid Game series, and it does a surprisingly good job recreating that experience. If you've watched the show, you'll recognize many of the games right away, which makes it even more enjoyable.

It's completely free, lightweight, and runs on almost any PC. The graphics are simple, but the gameplay is what makes it fun, especially when you're playing with friends and trying to survive until the end.

The only sad part is that the public servers aren't as active anymore. It was a lot more fun when the lobbies were full.

If you have a group of friends and you're a Squid Game fan, this is an easy recommendation. It's still a great time, even years later.

A free fun multiplayer experience based off of Netflix's Squid Game. Nothing of substance but the developer and community know it and that's what makes the game great: just a simple party game that you can pick up and drop whenever. While not many people play it now, during 2021 in its peak, it was fun to mess around and goof off with randoms for a few games.

This little Squid Game style game is fun, yes, but only for about the first five minutes. After that, it starts getting boring pretty quickly. I am not exactly a huge Roblox fan, but I have seen servers on that game offering the same kind of minigames in a much better way, which is not exactly a lifetime achievement award for this title.

That said, if you do not want to download Roblox and prefer something with a different structure from the usual “kids’ game” setup, it can still make some sense. It is simple, lightweight, and most importantly free, which always helps forgive a few sins.

The only real shame is that lately it seems to be heading toward eternal death: the servers look dangerously close to absolute zero, and the real minigame might soon be finding someone to play with.

citations.review_text:
👍 Recommended? Yes. Squid Game wishes it had this level of professionalism.

Crab Game proves one thing:

The cheaper the game...

The funnier the players.

Every lobby begins with everyone pretending to cooperate.

Within minutes, we've collectively returned to caveman society.

Trust lasts approximately three seconds.

Voice chat is responsible for 99% of the entertainment.

You'll hear:

"Guys, let's work together."

followed immediately by someone launching you off the map with the force of a freight train.

The physics have all the stability of shopping carts with square wheels.

That's exactly why they're perfect.

Winning feels great.

Watching twenty people accidentally eliminate themselves is somehow even better.

I've laughed harder playing this than games costing ten times as much.

10/10.

Humanity was a mistake.

This game is so much more than just a game involving crabs. It's a total masterpiece clearly made with real sweat, tears and other bodily fluids. When playing the game, you can really see that the developer, Dani, put a lot of time and effort into this work of art game that he has made which now at the time of me writing this has made a humungus impact on me, my self and I. 

Now that I'm here in my very own chair listening to musical music all i can think about is this wonderfully made art of work game. There are so many things that are good with it. As an example i can bring up the wonderfully integrated and moderated voicechat the Dani has offered us to us from him, Dani. It is such a good feature to be able to hear what all of the other players have to say about the game we are playing. Infact, I've learned so many new words from them, like the f and n word. 

In conclution I'd just like to say that this game should belong in some sort of art museum, like maybe the louvre in the country of paris in the country of europe. Or maybe after we have banished fish to the moon, we could make this game and all of its crabs repopulate the ocean and make the global trade better since no more fish would slow down the boats. And we would also get a bunch of wonderful Crab Game crabs in the oceans for all of us to enjoy. Which is totaly wonderful if you ask that question to me, the writer of these words. 

13 / 13 chainsaws

A fun game that changes the atmosphere from competitive play and other types of games. The game is funny, and you can use the microphone to talk to others on the server. You might encounter some toxic or hostile people, but it's good overall.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the voice chat as chaotic and filled with screaming players.

citations.review_text:
Crab Game is exactly what it looks like and somehow still delivers. The gameplay is simple, chaotic, and fun in all the right ways. But the real experience is the voice chat, which is less of a feature and more of a social experiment gone wrong. A beautiful, unhinged, completely unpredictable social experiment. Every lobby is a fresh batch of chaos filled with people who just discovered their microphone exists and have absolutely nothing valuable to contribute. It is genuinely one of the most entertaining things in gaming right now.

A couple of things to note:
1- The voice chat is 90% people who just hit puberty screaming into a 5 dollar headset and somehow that is part of the charm.
2- Do not expect a deep or polished experience. You are here for the memes and the madness, nothing else.
7/10 a hilarious and chaotic good time best enjoyed with friends. Just mute the randoms or embrace the noise, both are valid life choices.
Just a bunch of racist squeakers with soundboards being toxic. Would not recommend if you want to actually have fun in a game

Crab Game is basically what happens when you throw a bunch of people into a playground full of deadly children’s games and tell them “good luck not dying.” I’ve never played something so stupid, so chaotic, and somehow so entertaining at the same time.

The best part of Crab Game is that absolutely nothing is balanced, and honestly, that’s the charm. Every round feels like a physics experiment gone wrong. People slip, fall, shove each other off cliffs, or explode because they stood in the wrong spot for half a second. It’s the kind of game where skill matters… until someone randomly body-checks you into the shadow realm and laughs about it.

The chaos is unmatched. One moment you’re doing great, and the next the entire lobby decides you’re the one they’re sacrificing to the void. The maps are basically designed for betrayal, and the audio is… an experience. Half the fun is hearing 20 people panic-scream at once when the floor disappears or a bomb gets passed around like it’s hot potato on steroids.

But let’s be real, the game isn’t perfect. Public lobbies can be a mess, the physics are held together with duct tape, and sometimes you die because the universe decided it was “your turn.” It can get annoying, unfair, and absolutely ridiculous.

And yet? It’s hilarious.
Crab Game isn’t trying to be balanced or polished, it just wants you to suffer with friends in the funniest way possible. And honestly, it succeeds.

Booted up Crab Game thinking it was just “Squid Game but poor.”
It was actually therapy for my inner psychopath.

– Got screamed at in 14 different languages in 30 seconds
– Made more friends here than in real life (all of them betrayed me instantly)
– The jump physics are held together with duct tape and depression
– Pushed my best friend off a platform and whispered “worth it”
– Lobby chat is basically free cardio from laughing
– Survival of the loudest, not the fittest

10/10. I didn’t win a single round, but I did discover how good it feels to ruin someone else’s day.
